planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya obscura blooms most reliably when slightly pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya obscura is a Central American species with soft, gently fuzzy, dark green leaves on slender twining vines, producing small clusters of pale yellow-green, star-shaped flowers with a sweet fragrance, especially noticeable in the evening. Its modest, twining growth habit and smaller leaf size make it manageable in a hanging basket or on a small trellis without the bulk of larger-leaved hoya species. Provide a trellis or hanging basket for support, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs once they form, since hoya rebloom from the same spurs year after year.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya macrophylla needs more space than smaller hoya species due to its larger leaves and vigorous growth.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya macrophylla is a Southeast Asian species named for its notably large, broad, matte green leaves, considerably bigger than most commonly grown hoya, giving it a bolder, more substantial presence than the finer-textured hoya species typically grown as houseplants. Vigorous twining vines eventually produce rounded clusters of small, fragrant, cream to pale yellow flowers. Its larger leaves and faster growth mean it benefits from a sturdier trellis or larger hanging basket than compact hoya species. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and provide bright indirect light for the best growth, and never remove the woody flowering spurs.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya serpens is a cool-growing Himalayan species that prefers slightly cooler temperatures than many tropical hoya.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya serpens is a miniature Himalayan species with tiny, round, densely fuzzy silvery-green leaves packed closely along fine, wiry, trailing stems, giving it a delicate, mossy texture quite different from the larger, glossier leaves of most hoya. It produces small clusters of white, star-shaped flowers with a fine fringe of hairs. Being adapted to cooler mountain conditions, it appreciates slightly cooler nights and less intense heat than typical tropical hoya, and benefits from excellent drainage to prevent its fine roots from rotting. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and grow in a small pot or shallow dish where the trailing stems can be admired up close.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya finlaysonii blooms most reliably when slightly pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya finlaysonii carries thick, rounded, dark green leaves with prominently sunken venation that gives the surface a quilted, almost padded texture, a distinctive look among hoya species most known for smooth, glossy foliage. Twining vines produce rounded clusters of star-shaped, cream to pale yellow flowers with a fine fringe of hairs on the corona. Its sturdy, thick leaves store water well and make it relatively forgiving of missed waterings compared to thinner-leaved hoya. Provide a trellis or hanging basket for support, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya vitiensis blooms most reliably when slightly pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya vitiensis is a Fijian species with thick, glossy, deep green leaves on vigorous twining vines, producing rounded clusters of waxy, star-shaped flowers typical of the genus. Its sturdy, substantial leaves and steady growth make it a reliable, relatively low-maintenance hoya for a bright window or covered porch. Provide a trellis or hanging basket for the twining stems, let the chunky potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs once they form, since blooms return from the same spurs year after year.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya callistophylla is a slower-growing collector species that rewards patience with dramatic foliage.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya callistophylla is prized above almost all other hoya species for its dramatic foliage rather than its flowers, with long, dark green to near-black leaves marked by bold, bright white to pale yellow-green venation running the length of each leaf, an effect striking enough to rival any patterned aroid. Twining vines eventually produce clusters of small, waxy flowers, but growers seek this species out primarily for the leaf pattern. It is slower-growing and somewhat more particular about consistent warmth and humidity than easier hoya species. Provide a trellis or hanging basket for support, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and give bright indirect light to maintain the sharp leaf-vein contrast.

common_name: Compacta Hoya (Hindu Rope Plant, Curly Wax Plant)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Compacta blooms most reliably when quite pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Compacta, widely sold as Hindu Rope Plant, is one of the most distinctive hoya cultivars, with thick, waxy leaves that curl and twist tightly around themselves along densely congested stems, forming a dense, ropy, cascading cord unlike the flat, open growth of standard wax plant. Established plants produce rounded, ball-shaped clusters of small, fragrant, waxy pink to red-centered flowers from the same reusable flowering spurs, which should never be trimmed off. Its slow growth and dense habit suit it well to a small hanging basket where the twisted, cascading stems can be fully appreciated. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and provide bright indirect light for the best growth.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Exotica holds its heavier silver variegation best with consistent bright indirect light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix. Exotica carries even heavier, more continuous silver splashing across its thick, quilted, heart-shaped leaves than the similar Silvery Ann cultivar, so that some leaves can appear nearly all silver with only patches of the dark green base color remaining, giving it a frostier, more metallic overall look. The satin-textured leaf surface catches light distinctively, and the trailing or climbing vine works equally well in a hanging basket or trained up a moss pole. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings, since scindapsus is prone to root rot in constantly wet soil, and provide bright indirect light to keep the heavy variegation from reverting toward plain green.
